title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Appropriate Equipment & Instrumentation - Biotechnology - pH meters, analytical balances
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: After successfully utilizing a digital pH meter to adjust the acidity of a Tris-HCl buffer, the laboratory technician must properly clean and store the fragile glass electrode. To actively maintain the electrolytic integrity of the electrode's internal reference junction, how must the glass bulb be stored overnight?
options: Completely dry, exposed to ambient laboratory air on the benchtop to effectively prevent microbial growth.
Fully immersed in pure, high-resistance deionized (DI) water.
Fully immersed in a dedicated high-concentration salt storage solution, typically $3 \text{ M}$ Potassium Chloride (KCl).
Fully immersed in $100\%$ absolute ethanol to rapidly dehydrate and sterilize the porous glass matrix.
questions.explain:
A pH probe operates via a delicate internal salt solution (usually Potassium Chloride) that interacts with the sample through a microscopic porous junction in the glass bulb. 

If the probe is stored dry (Option 'a'), the bulb cracks and the internal salt dries out, destroying the electrode. If it is stored in DI water (Option 'b'), osmosis will violently pull the ions out of the internal solution, rendering the probe deaf to voltage changes. Therefore, it must be stored in a matching, ion-rich **electrode storage solution** (typically $3 \text{ M}$ or $4 \text{ M}$ KCl) to preserve the junction's ionic balance.

questions.q: A quality control technician is operating a highly sensitive analytical balance, attempting to weigh out exactly $1.5000 \text{ g}$ of a fine chemical powder. The digital readout on the balance is highly unstable, constantly fluctuating randomly between $1.4985 \text{ g}$ and $1.5032 \text{ g}$ over a period of three minutes. Which of the following is the most likely physical cause of this measurement instability?
options: The technician inadvertently left the sliding glass draft shield doors open, allowing imperceptible room air currents to strike and push against the weighing pan.
The ambient laboratory humidity has dropped significantly below $80\%$, causing the crystalline powder to undergo rapid and violent sublimation.
The technician foolishly used a lightweight plastic weigh boat instead of a heavy-duty borosilicate glass beaker.
The specific chemical powder possesses a localized magnetic field that is actively short-circuiting the balance's internal digital motherboard.
questions.explain:
Analytical balances are engineered to be sensitive down to fractions of a milligram ($0.0001 \text{ g}$). 

Because of this extreme sensitivity, the physical downward force of a minor air current (such as HVAC vents, someone walking by, or simply warm air rising) is sufficient to wildly alter the readings on the weighing pan. This is exactly why all analytical balances are encased in a **glass draft shield**, and all measurements must be taken with the sliding doors completely shut to seal out atmospheric disturbances.

questions.q: A standard operating procedure (SOP) explicitly instructs a researcher to place a clean weigh boat on the balance pan and press the "Tare" (or "Zero") button prior to adding their powdered chemical. What is the precise quantitative function of executing this "Tare" command?
options: It actively recalibrates the balance's internal load cell against standard regional gravity constants based on geographic location.
It mathematically instructs the balance to subtract the exact empty weight of the container, ensuring only the true net mass of the added chemical is recorded.
It forces the digital display unit to seamlessly convert internal data from Imperial units (ounces) to standard SI metric units (grams).
It electrically heats the weighing pan for five seconds to thoroughly evaporate any ambient microscopic moisture condensed on the surface.
questions.explain:
When preparing chemical solutions, scientists need to know the mass of the chemical alone, without including the weight of the plastic weigh boat or beaker holding it. 

Pressing the **Tare** (or Zero) button electronically subtracts the current mass sitting on the pan, resetting the digital display to exactly $0.000 \text{ g}$. When the chemical powder is subsequently added to the container, the balance calculates only the newly added net mass, simplifying the procedure and minimizing arithmetic errors.
